summary: A left press on the search scope bar no longer moves the keyboard. One mouse-down listener on the bar's container in src/finder/bars.rs (render_scope_bar) calls window.prevent_default(), so the Finder's root div, the nearest element that tracks a focus handle, does not take the keyboard as GPUI's divs do on any press. Before that, when the root itself already has the keyboard, or the keyboard is outside this browser (split view's other pane, or an element that is no longer drawn), the listener gives it to this browser's files. Nothing else in src changed (15 lines). The brief's cause was wrong in two details and the code was followed instead: the kit's input does not blur itself on a press outside it, and the keyboard did not go to nothing or to the window's root but to the Finder's own root, where shortcuts still worked and only letters and the files' keys were dead.
changelog: A click on This Computer, the folder's name, Name, or Contents in the search scope bar took the keyboard away from the search field, or from the files, and gave it to nothing: letters typed next were lost, and the arrow keys did nothing, until you clicked the field or a file or pressed Cmd+F. The keyboard now stays where it was, so you can switch to Contents and go on typing, or press Down Arrow to move into the results. It stays in the filter field the same way. Search Syntax opened with the bar's (i) button gives the keyboard back to the search field when it closes, and a Return or Down Arrow that is waiting for the results still moves into them after a click in the bar. When nothing had the keyboard, the click gives it to the files, and in split view a click in the other pane's scope bar gives it to that pane's files.
behaviour_changes: A click on This Computer, the folder's name, Name or Contents in the search scope bar leaves the keyboard in the search field: typing goes on in the field, and Down Arrow or Return move into the results, also when they are pressed before the results are in.

With the keyboard in the files, such a click leaves it there: the arrow keys and the other file keys go on working. The selection is let go when the answer comes, as results-scroll-reset has it, so Down Arrow then goes to the first result.
With the keyboard in the filter field or in the Nushell panel's field, it stays there (the filter field is tested; the Nushell panel was probed by the implementer and again in review).

When the browser as a whole had the keyboard (after a click on the status bar, or on a Smart Folder in the sidebar's list; both probed in review), a click in the bar gives it to the files. Before, it stayed dead.

Split view: a click in the other pane's scope bar gives the keyboard to that pane's files. Before, it went to that pane as a whole, where shortcuts worked but arrows and typing did not. Probed in review in both directions, and for the funnel (that pane's filter field) and (i) (that pane's files after the dialog).

The bar's blank parts and the "Search:" label behave like the chips: the keyboard stays where it was, or goes to the files when nothing had it. Before, a click there took it away. Probed in review; no kept test.

Search Syntax opened with the bar's (i) gives the keyboard back to the field it came from when it closes: the search field (tested), and by the same code the filter field or the Nushell panel's field. Cmd+/ already did this. Before, it ended in the files.

A click on a chip while the Kind menu is open closes the menu and does its work as before, and the keyboard is back in the search field. Before, it was lost. The same after a toolbar menu such as Sort (probed in review). After an item's context menu the keyboard goes to the files, where it was before the menu.

A Return or Down Arrow that is waiting for results goes on waiting through a click in the bar and moves into what the click found. Before, the click called it off by taking the keyboard away. The toolbar's Search Only in button already left it waiting (probed in review as well). A click on the funnel or on (i) still calls it off, because the keyboard goes to the filter field or to the dialog.

A click in the bar while a name is being edited in place ends the edit as before, keeping what was typed, and the keyboard is then in the files (tested, added in review), or in the sidebar's tree for a name edited there (probed in review), instead of lost. A name that was refused goes on being edited, as before.
A press on the bar that is not released there no longer moves the keyboard (by the code, not tested).
The same in a file chooser (--pick): probed in review, no chooser-specific code.

Manual, Searching: the scope bar's lead-in reads "While a search is active, the scope bar shows the controls below. A click on This Computer, "Folder name", Name, or Contents leaves the keyboard where it was, so you can go on typing in the search field or moving through the results with the arrow keys."
Unchanged: the funnel (the filter field when it opens the bar, the files when it closes it), the Kind button and its menu, the filter bar's own buttons, the toolbar, and right or middle presses.
left_out: CHANGELOG.md is not edited, per the guide. The entry is in this record and in the commit message.

The Kind button is untouched. Its popover trigger stops the press before the bar's listener sees it, and its menu gives the keyboard back to wherever it was: to nothing when nothing had it, and to the other pane in split view (both probed in review). The toolbar's menus do the same, and the brief says not to fight a menu's own restore.

Only the left button is handled, like the kit's buttons. A right or middle press on a chip still gives the keyboard to the browser as a whole (probed in review: a letter typed after a right press is lost).
The funnel closing the filter bar still moves the keyboard to the files: close_filter always does, as Cmd+Alt+F and the filter bar's close button do.

The filter bar: its own controls (Save, the close button) are kit Buttons and never had the fault, so nothing was changed there. Its blank parts (the funnel icon, the word "where") still take the keyboard away, like the toolbar's title, the status bar and the path bar.

No kept test for the bar's blank parts, the file chooser, the Nushell panel's field, or a name edited in the sidebar's tree. Each was probed in review with a throwaway test and goes through the same listener as a tested case.
cargo clippy --features term was not run: src/term is untouched and no signature changed.

Not compiled for macOS or Windows. The change has no cfg-specific code and uses only FocusHandle::is_focused and contains_focused, Window::prevent_default, and the MouseButton and MouseDownEvent this file already used.
README.md and the Search Syntax dialog are unchanged: neither states anything this affects.

review_fixes: Added tests/controls.rs a_click_in_the_scope_bar_ends_a_rename_with_the_keyboard_in_the_files. The implementer had probed this and kept no test. It is the one place where leaving the keyboard where it is would be wrong: the name's field must not go on taking keys after the click. It works because the field ends its own edit in the capture phase of the same press (on_mouse_down_out in inline_rename.rs), before the bar's listener looks at where the keyboard is. The test renames a search result, clicks the folder chip, and expects the chip to have done its work, the typed name on disk, no field, and the keyboard in the files. Seen failing without the change at the last of these.

notes:
Checked. With the src diff reverse-applied on the final commit, all ten tests listed fail, each for the reason given, and scope_bar_controls and scope_bar_tooltips_name_their_shortcuts pass either way. Three mutations of the listener, one at a time: without the is_focused clause only a_click_in_the_scope_bar_gives_the_files_a_keyboard_that_was_nowhere fails; without the contains_focused clause only the split view test; with the files always given the keyboard, the typing, filter field, Kind menu and Search Syntax tests and return_goes_on_waiting_through_a_switch_to_contents fail. check.sh printed CHECK OK on the trunk commit: 510 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures. The ten tests and the other Return tests of tests/finder.rs also pass with SEED=0, 1, 7, 42, 99 and 1234, and with the window made active first (ui.activate()), where focus and blur events fire as they do in the real app; the tests as kept run in an inactive window. After 40f8e86 (search-truncation-honesty) landed on top, the same tests pass on that tip. I looked at the window myself: after Cmd+F, "bud", a click on Contents and "get", the field reads "budget" and still has its focus ring (review-typing.png); after one more click on the folder chip and Down Arrow, the first result is selected in the active colour and the ring has left the field (review-down-dark.png).

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt someone, and what the code says. (1) The keyboard is left in something that should have let go of it. A name being edited ends its own edit in the capture phase of the same press, so by the time the bar's listener looks the keyboard is in the files or in the tree, and a refused name goes on being edited as before (probed both, in the files and in the sidebar's tree; one test kept). A waiting Return or Down Arrow stands through the click; set_scope, set_kind and set_search_contents never called it off, only the lost keyboard did, and the first answer of the new search clears the selection before the move, so the first result is what gets selected. (2) The files are given a keyboard that something else should keep, since contains_focused reads the last drawn frame and 'outside this browser' covers more than the other pane. A dialog covers the bar, so no press reaches it while a dialog has the keyboard (probed: a click where the Contents chip is, with Search Syntax open, closes the dialog and does not reach the chip). A menu closes in the capture phase and hands the keyboard back before the listener looks, and neither PopupMenu::dismiss nor the popover's close takes it back afterwards: both first look at where the keyboard is. While a dialog is animating out the kit has blurred the window and restores its own target on a timer, exactly as it did when the root took the keyboard. An element that is focused but no longer drawn counts as outside, and the files are the right place then. (3) prevent_default on the whole bar stops something that needs the press. In gpui-pre 0.3.10 the flag is read by the focus-on-press listeners of ancestors and by their pressed state, and by touch handling; nothing above the bar has a pressed style, the bar is not a window drag area, the platform layers don't read it, and the bar's children run before its listener. The Kind trigger stops the press before the bar sees it, and a disabled Kind button does too.

Doubts that remain, for the owner. (a) The waiting Return. It now stands through a click in the bar and moves into the new results, as it does through the toolbar's Search Only in button and through the Kind menu. If a click in the bar should call it off instead, add `this.enter_results = None;` to the listener in render_scope_bar and turn return_goes_on_waiting_through_a_switch_to_contents around. (b) Kind is the one control in the bar that neither rescues a keyboard that was nowhere nor brings it to its pane in split view: its menu gives the keyboard back to wherever it was. A capture-phase listener on the bar could change that; I left it, because the brief says not to fight a menu's restore and the toolbar's menus behave the same. (c) Only the left button is handled. A right or middle press on a chip still loses the keyboard, as it does everywhere on the chrome. on_any_mouse_down in place of on_mouse_down(MouseButton::Left, ..) would cover them. (d) The whole bar keeps the keyboard, its blank parts and the "Search:" label included, which the brief did not ask for; no test pins it. (e) Nothing was run on macOS or Windows.

For briefs still to come.
- focus-lost-recovery: independent. This only stops a press on the scope bar from moving the keyboard, and never makes the focused element go undrawn. When the focused element is gone, contains_focused is false, so a press on the bar gives the files the keyboard, the same place your handler puts it.
- escape-ends-search: toolbar.rs is untouched. After a click on a chip the keyboard is still in the search field, so Escape there acts as you plan: the first press clears the field, the next one moves to the files.
- split-active-pane: a press on a pane's scope bar puts the keyboard in that pane's files unless it was already somewhere in that pane, so a contains_focused sync in Workspace::render sees that pane. The exception is the Kind menu, which gives the keyboard back to the pane it came from, as the toolbar's menus do. The scope bar's IDs repeat in both panes: click in the split pane with click_in("split-pane", ..); the first pane has no wrapper with an ID, so a probe has to click by position (find_all and the leftmost).
- regex-content-search, smart-folder-save-and-leaks, and anything else that adds a control to render_scope_bar: the bar's container has the mouse-down listener, so a plain element (the `chip` closure) needs nothing of its own; its press leaves the keyboard where it was. A kit Button refuses the keyboard on a left press by itself, and its press still reaches the bar's listener. A popover trigger stops the press, so its menu restores the keyboard to wherever it was. A text field in the bar would still take the keyboard: it focuses itself before the bar's listener looks, and the listener leaves alone whatever is inside the browser. A dialog opened from the bar now returns the keyboard to the field it came from (focus_before_dialog looks for a focused field).
- recent-searches: if set_scope gets a window parameter, its two callers in bars.rs are the chips' click listeners just below the new on_mouse_down in render_scope_bar.
- empty-state-messages: your plan says a clicked kit Button takes the keyboard and that the scope and kind handlers must call focus_files. A left click does not give a kit Button the keyboard (gpui-component button.rs calls prevent_default on the press), and the chips in the scope bar now leave the keyboard where it was. If your handlers call focus_files every time, a click on a button in the message takes the keyboard out of the search field while the chip above it, which does the same job, does not. Give the files the keyboard only when the button itself has it (reached with Tab) or nothing in the browser does; the listener in render_scope_bar has that test.
- search-syntax-click-example: closing_search_syntax_gives_the_keyboard_back_to_the_search_field clicks search-help, then help-done, then types a letter and expects it in the search field. If clicking an example closes the dialog and fills the field, keep help-done or change that test with it.
- kind-filter-single-list: the_kind_menu_gives_the_keyboard_back_to_the_search_field clicks `kind` and the menu item "Folder"; keep the label or change the test.
- history-menus: independent. What you may meet: a right press on an enabled kit Button gives the button itself the keyboard (seen on the scope bar's Kind button), which is why your prevent_default for the right button is needed.
- inactive-selection-colour: after a click on a chip the files keep the keyboard, or get it, so their selection is drawn as active.
- image-preview-details, path-bar-no-io, split-view-toolbar-clip, regex-content-search, and anyone who changes what a click on blank chrome does: a_click_in_the_scope_bar_gives_the_files_a_keyboard_that_was_nowhere clicks `status-text` to leave the keyboard with the browser as a whole, and asserts that it did. If a click there stops doing that, change the test's setup, not its end. It still holds on 40f8e86, which gave the count a tooltip.
- tab-bar-overflow, split-view-toolbar-clip, preview-card-height: nothing in the bar's layout changed.

Found, not fixed (all there before this change).
- After a click on a Smart Folder or any other row of the sidebar's list, and after a click on blank chrome (the status bar, the toolbar's title, the path bar, the filter bar's blank parts), the keyboard is with the browser as a whole: shortcuts work, but arrows and typing do nothing until a file or a field is clicked. This is the fault this brief fixes for the scope bar, everywhere else. Probed for a Smart Folder and the status bar. One fix at the root, such as giving the files the keyboard whenever the Finder's own focus handle gets it, would cover them all; the is_focused half of the test in the bar's listener would then never be true, and the test that pins it would need another way to reach that state.
- A right or middle press on the chrome takes the keyboard away the same way. On an enabled kit Button it gives the keyboard to the button itself, where Return and Space then press it.
- With nothing in the browser holding the keyboard, a menu (Kind, Sort, Actions) gives it back to nothing when it closes.
